_about: SMOKE class — deliberately tiny, no dimension derivation: two hand-runnable scenes for tire-kicking the record→dashboard loop itself. When the process feels right, real classes (CHIPDROP etc.) take over and SMOKE stays as the 30-second 'is the board basically alive' check.
title: Board smoke checks — quick hand-run scenes to exercise the QA loop

hard_assertions: your eyes, following the steps — this class exists to exercise the recording loop, not the automation
oracle.trace_shape: kdiag captures the board activity between your test:start and test:verdict automatically

instances.title: Board loads clean
instances.steps:
1. Open a live game board (e.g. lab1 /m/katomia/game/t-prop) on any device.
2. Wait ~3 seconds for the chips to settle.
3. Check: every chip visible (none off-screen, none under the header or footer); no two chips heavily overlapping; ghosts sitting on the rim; hub + footer present; board perfectly STILL once settled.
4. Pass if all true. Note anything odd even on a pass.

instances.title: Drop one chip to a neighbour (and take it back)
instances.steps:
1. On the same board, drag a fungible chip (e.g. some ℏ) from your store onto a NEIGHBOURING player's segment; give an amount.
2. Check: a pale ghost appears on YOUR rim; the chip lands in their basket; hovering shows the dotted pile→ghost→basket line, all three points ON their chips.
3. Nudge test: watch 5 seconds — nothing else on the board should have jumped.
4. Withdraw the offer (drag it back / withdraw). Check everything returns and the lines clear.
5. Pass if all true.

fixtures.manual: any live board on lab1; kdiag records around your run automatically
